notes: and how the parking lot items will be addressed. He noted the various reports included on today’s agenda, including the 2024 fees and charges by-law, the staffing strategy, the urban forestry update and the corporate business plan.

notes: 6. Budget Overview

6.1 Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview and summary, including asset management, general budget information and the public engagement process undertaken.

Mark Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer provided an overview of the tax supported operating budget, including operating budget facts and how the budget works, funding challenges, significant formatting changes, contributions to capital and impact areas.
A. McNabb reviewed the Debt Analysis, debt payments by service type and projected debt as a percentage of revenue.
Staff responded to questions regarding user fees for recreation programming, impact of lower OLG funding during pandemic, funding for new positions, and total capital funds for recreation.
Deputy Mayor Wilton called for a recess and reconvened at 10:40am.
7. Consideration of Reports
7.1 2024 Fees and Charges By-Law
Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer
A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report.

Councillor Jefferson requested moving the decision on the fees and charges by-law to the parking lot for further discussion related to the content of the operating budget, Members of Council agreed to defer consideration of Fees and Charges By-law to the parking lot.
Deputy Mayor Wilton indicated staff requested the Corporate Business plan be consideration after the Draft Budget.
7.2 Staffing Strategy
Presentation by D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer & R. Hasan, Chief Human Resources Officer

Rashid Hasan, Chief Human Resources Officer provided an overview of the staffing strategy, including the guiding principles, the compensation philosophy, the justification process, and the learning and development program.

D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer outlined the staffing strategy funding formula, the 2024 proposed new staffing and the funding strategy for 10.6 FTEs. Staff responded to questions regarding the continued hiring of students, the timing for the hiring of the gardener and facility attendant, the secondment of a current employee for the Operations Centre project manager, the role of the climate change coordinator, the customer service associate at the Jefferson Elora Community Centre, and the function of the future landscape architect planner.
7.3 Living Wage Employer
Presentation by A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report, indicating the certificate process and a recommendation to conduct a more fulsome review as part of the 2026-27 market compensation review.
7.4 Urban Forestry Update
Report from L. Rogerson, Manager of Parks
Lucas Rogerson, Manager of Parks provided an overview of the report, highlighting the adopted Public Forest Policy, and the recently adopted Public Tree By-law.

L. Rogerson responded to questions regarding continuing work and fostering relationships with local community groups, termites, exploring the planting of fruit trees, and removal of invasive species such as Buckthorn.

Colin Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services responded to questions regarding tree replacement and applicable ratios, increasing plantings and other green components to construction projects, the commemorative tree program, and development of a private tree by-law.
7.5 2024 Corporate Business Plan
Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer
Item moved to 12.2
8. Delegations
8.1 Fergus Business Improvement Area (BIA) Budget Presentation Councillor Jefferson, having declared a conflict of interest with respect to the Fergus BIA, left the meeting.

Fred Gordon, Fergus BIA Administrator thanked and recognized Deputy Mayor Wilton, Township staff Kristen Drexler, Kerri O’Kane, Mark Bradey and others from Public Works and CW Hydro for their help and assistance. F. Gordon outlined the various exciting and successful events, including movie night, Tartan Day, Medieval Fair and many others. He outlined the various beautification projects, including the Provost pavilion, flowers, rotating flag program and public sculptures.

F. Gordon noted the importance of weekly garbage collection and the significant costs associated with private garbage collection. The BIA is grateful for the Township’s financial assistance and is committed to working with both the Township and the County of Wellington to find a permanent, cost-effective solution to garbage in the downtown.
F. Gordon indicated to continue to expand events, programs and beautification projects, there will be a 4% increase to the levy.

8.2 Elora Business Improvement (BIA) Area Budget Presentation MacLean Hann, Elora BIA Chair echoed the comments of Fred Gordon and expressed his gratitude on behalf of the Elora BIA for the hard work of Councillors and staff, making all efforts very worthwhile. He provided an overview of the food events, including, Eloralisious, Elora Burger Battle, and Food Day Canada. He highlighted other events and activities such as Starlight Shopping, Candlelight Elora, and purchasing more lights to brighten the streets.
M. Hann noted the burden of the garbage costs and missed pick ups.
He also noted the main focus for the BIA in 2024 will be the updating of the Christmas lights for the hydro posts which is the rational for the $50,000 loan from the Township.
9. Budget Overview Continued
9.1 Tax Supported Operating Budget

M. Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer provided an overview of the 2024 tax supported operating budget summary. He reviewed the average residential tax bill breakdown and noted the significant areas impacting the tax supported operating budget.
Councillor Jefferson requested adding to the parking lot the phasing in of the Councillor salary increase over two years.

Staff responded to questions regarding the increase to conferences and communications, costs associated with animal control, user fees related to false alarms, relocation of the Cemetery Administrator, and the LCBO lease.
Deputy Mayor Wilton called for a 5-minute recess, the meeting resumed at 2:40pm.

9.2 Capital Budget - Bridges, Replacement Schedule and 10 year forecast M. Bradey provided a brief overview and staff responded to questions regarding the office retrofits, the 205 Queen Street renovations, Tourism office renovations, and potential options for ice resurfacers.
9.3 Parking Lot Items
D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer outlined the thirteen (13) Parking Lot Items (outlined in Appendix B to report COR2023-112 and those added by Council).
1. Delegation - Elora Centre for the Arts;
2. Delegation - Randy Vaine re Bylaw Enforcement;
3. Suggestion from a Member Council re use of OLG funds to offset costs of termite management;
4. Delegation - Fergus Tennis Club;
5. Delegation - Greenlanes re capital budget;
6. Greenlanes re: active transportation;
7. Greenlanes re: parking lot at Jefferson Elora Community Centre;
8. 11 reduction items proposed by staff
9. Fees and Charges By-law;
10. Phasing in salary increase for Mayor and Councillors over two years;
11. Fergus Grand Theatre;

items.title: Elora BIA budget – requested for an interest free loan.
notes: Mayor Watters declared a conflict of interest with respect to parking lot item 1 regarding the request for funding from the Elora Centre for the Arts.
After considerable discussion, the following resolutions were put forward:
Mayor Watters, having declared a conflict of interest with respect to the Elora Centre for the Arts, left the room and did not participate in the discussions or the vote.
10. ADJOURNMENT
10.1 Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer noted at the end of Day 1, after reductions, the current tax rate was now sitting at 7.52%.
11. Budget Overview Continued
11.1 Parking Lot Continued
Deputy Mayor Wilton called the meeting to order, indicating Council will begin with consideration of the Fees and Charges By-law (previously deferred to the Parking Lot)
A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview, indicating Council had given direction to staff to set the increase at 6.0%.
Councillor Jefferson put forth the suggestion to raise the user fees for Parks & Recreation to 6.5% or 7%.
After a lengthy discussion, there was no interest in raising the overall user fees beyond the recommended 6%.
After discussion on the temporary washrooms in Elora, and the suggestion that alternative funding sources be explored, the following resolution was put forward:
After discussion on the temporary washrooms in Elora, and the suggestion that alternative funding sources be explored, the following resolution was put forward:
Councillor Jefferson suggested phasing in the salary increase for Mayor and Council over the next two years to reduce the impact on 2024.

Councillor Jefferson spoke to the activity and revenue generated through the Fergus Grand Theatre. P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services suggested work was underway on the update to the Culture Action Plan and indicated staff would be happy to report on future profitability for the theatre.
Councillor Adams suggested taking a closer look at the Environmental Services budget for potential reductions.
D. Wilson indicated reduction to the Environmental Services budget, funded through fixed water and wastewater rates, will not result in an impact to the overall operating budget.

Deputy Mayor Wilton indicated the final item on the “parking lot” is the request from the Elora BIA for a $50,000 interest free loan. Staff responded to questions regarding the term of the loan and the zero impact to the tax supported budget.
D. Wilson, CAO provided a summary of the reductions, which included 5 of the 11 reductions proposed by staff:
 Use of 3% of OLG Funds for termite management;
 Increase in revenue for the committee of adjustment;
 Investment income increase;

 Reduction in the transfer to capital (asset management); and  Removal of the rental of temporary washrooms in Elora He also indicated Council has directed the salary increase for Members of Council to be phased in over 2024 and 2025.
A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer confirmed the resultant tax rate for 2024 currently is 7.38%.
12. Budget Deliberations
12.1 Ontario Regulation 284/09 - 2024 Budget

Report from M. Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington adopt Report No. COR2023-111 regarding additional financial disclosure requirements for the 2024 budget year pursuant to Ontario Regulation 284/09.
Deputy Mayor Wilton called for a 10 minute recess, the meeting resumed at 10:15 am.
12.2 2024 Corporate Business Plan
Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer

Mayor Watters having declared a conflict of interest with respect to matters involving the Elora Centre for the Arts left the room and therefore did not participate in the discussion on the next item nor did he vote on the matter.

D. Wilson, CAO indicated the 2024 Corporate Business Plan should be amended to include the direction given directing staff to initiate discussions with the Elora Centre for the Arts regarding opportunities for collaboration and support, and report back to Council.
D. Wilson, CAO outlined the various amendments required to the Corporate Business Plan as a result of Council direction as follows:
a) Remove Item # 2 (Page 9), Retrofit Tourism Office space to improve visitor experience and staff workspaces;
b) Add Item #17 (Page 17), Install seating area heating at the Sportsplex (Pad B);
c) Add Item # 18 (Page 17), Install basketball nets at the Sportsplex Hall;
d) Add Item # 7 (Page 11) Investigate the profitability of the Fergus Grand Theatre;

D. Wilson and B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning & Development, responded to questions regarding the Parking Strategy, the investigation of a Community Planning Permit System, the elimination of exclusionary zoning and updating the Township’s Official Plan.
12.3 2024 Draft Budget
Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided a summary and indicated staff will make adjustments to the budget book based on the direction and will bring forward a by-law for Council’s consideration at the December 18th meeting.
13. Adjourn
